patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — commercetools and Medusa share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

commercetools and Medusa share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits. Choose commercetools only if your buying job matches “Composable enterprise commerce API — quote-only packages + 60-day free trial; contact sale” rather than Medusa's shape. Choose Medusa only if your buying job matches “Headless JS commerce — MIT OSS free; Cloud Develop $29, Launch $99 highlighted, Scale $299” rather than commercetools's shape. Workflow advantage: commercetools leans wholesale-b2b; Medusa leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — commercetools and Medusa share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: commercetools is Composable enterprise commerce API — quote-only packages + 60-day free trial; contact sales. Shopify keeps the SaaS award.; Medusa is Headless JS commerce — MIT OSS free; Cloud Develop $29, Launch $99 highlighted, Scale $299, Enterprise custom. No GMV tax..
- Company-size focus: commercetools (mid-market, enterprise) vs Medusa (small-business, mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: commercetools-leaning wholesale-b2b vs Medusa-leaning —.
- Researched limits: commercetools — No published monthly list price — hard to compare without a sales worksheet; Medusa — Headless means you still build or buy the storefront UX.

Limitations — commercetools: No published monthly list price — hard to compare without a sales worksheet; Requires front-end / MACH assembly — not a weekend theme launch; Medusa: Headless means you still build or buy the storefront UX; Not a WordPress-native plugin path (see WooCommerce).

Poor-fit cases: commercetools is a poor fit when that limitation bites: No published monthly list price — hard to compare without a sales worksheet · Medusa is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Headless means you still build or buy the storefront UX · Avoid commercetools if you actually need Medusa's motion (Headless JS commerce — MIT OSS free; Cloud Develop $29, Launch $99 highlighted, )

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
